ASCII and pixel art on gno.land, rendered rather than described:
[**the gallery**](/r/moul/gallery).

It stores nothing. Every piece lives where its author put it, and the gallery
renders the ones it can import and points at the ones it cannot. Settler #25 is
there, and the generators: gnoface, millipede, sapin.

Every page also answers to `?fmt=txt`, which is the same document built for a
terminal instead of a browser: no markdown syntax, links as numbered footnotes,
columns that line up. Try
[the index as plain text](/r/moul/gallery:?fmt=txt).

On mygnoscan: :scan.links:

- **One package a day**, under `x/daily`: small and finished, each one a
  question about what Gno can express, answered. The current count is in
  Packages below, because a number typed here would be wrong by next week.
- **[mygnoscan](https://github.com/gnoverse/mygnoscan)**, an explorer for gno
  chains. It is the only one that distinguishes a package that is live from one
  that was uploaded and is still waiting to be approved.
- **[A blog that is a realm](/r/moul/blog).** Every post is an entry in an
  on-chain store, published by a transaction. Same trick as this page.
- **Mainnet.** gno.land is launched. The interesting part is no longer the
  chain, it is what is running on it.
- **[Bubble Rumble](https://bubblerumble.net/?ref=g1manfred47kzduec920z88wfr64ylksmdcedlf5).**
  Jae Kwon's last-boop-wins pot game, real GNOT on mainnet, with a whole
  multiplayer client grown around it in a week. That link is my invite: boop
  through it and we both earn its BUBBLE token.

276 packages of mine are live on mainnet, from [moul/gno-contracts](https://github.com/moul/gno-contracts).
